paragraphs: Barnet Council's own fostering service and the independent agencies that list Barnet as an area they cover are all shown above. Fostering for the council means caring for Barnet's own children, with the council's social workers supporting you. An independent agency assesses, approves and supervises you itself, and councils, Barnet among them, ask agencies to find homes for children they cannot place with their own carers.

Barnet does not recruit on its own. It is one of six councils, with Camden, Enfield, Hackney, Haringey and Islington, in the North London Fostering Hub, which Camden hosts and which opened on Thursday 1 October. The hub builds on the North London Fostering and Permanency Consortium, through which the six boroughs have shared training, resources and recruitment since 2012, and its stated aim is to help more children stay close to their schools, friends and support networks. The government has also said its Room Makers programme, which helps carers adapt their homes so they can take more children, will be extended to every fostering hub.

The council's placement sufficiency strategy for 2023 to 2027 sets out which children most need homes. It puts growing in-house fostering among its priorities, noting that at the end of 2022 just over a quarter of Barnet's children in care (27.6%) lived with the council's own foster carers. It names vulnerable teenagers, including young people with mental health difficulties, a disability or neurodiversity, and those at risk of exploitation or going missing. It records 22 parent and child placements over a year, with five or six running at any one time, and says larger groups of brothers and sisters came into care in 2021/22. In that year one in five children in Barnet's care (20.4%) were unaccompanied asylum-seeking children.

If you could offer a home to a teenager, to a parent with a baby, or to siblings who want to stay together, say so when you first call: these are the needs the council's strategy names. Ask each service how it trains and supports carers for those placements and what it pays, as allowances and fees differ between the council and agencies.

Speak to the council and the agencies above before you decide. Barnet borders several areas with their own pages, so if you live near the edge of the borough, the Enfield, Haringey, Brent, Harrow and Hertfordshire pages, and the page for London as a whole, list more services nearby.
